items.detail: The **S&P 500 ground out a net gain to close the week at 7,489.72** (from ~7,413 Monday), but the path was violent — the Dow suffered its **worst day since April 2025** on Fed day before an Amazon-led Friday rebound left the index modestly higher.
items.why: Early-week disinflation optimism gave way to a hawkish Fed and an oil shock mid-week, then blowout cloud earnings pulled the tape back up into the weekly close.

items.detail: The Fed held at **3.50%–3.75% in a hawkish 9–3 vote** with three officials dissenting for a hike, sending the **30-year yield to its highest since 2007** and triggering a 2.19% Dow rout.
items.why: The hike dissents and Warsh's 'inflation too high' message gutted rate-cut hopes and repriced the curve toward tightening just as oil re-spiked.

items.detail: Megacap earnings split the tape along the AI-capex fault line: **Amazon soared ~15% (AWS +37% to $42.2B)** and Microsoft jumped ~7% on 43% Azure growth, while **Apple plunged ~7.4%** (shedding ~$500B) and Meta slid on a 91% free-cash-flow collapse.
items.why: Accelerating cloud revenue reframed AI spend as demand-driven, but Apple's data-center-driven supply-chain and margin warning showed the same boom straining hardware.

items.detail: Indian equities finished the week higher, with the **Nifty climbing from ~23,996 to above 24,350** and the **Sensex nearing 78,000**, decoupling from a hostile global backdrop of surging U.S. yields and rebounding oil.
items.why: A domestic-led rally and heavy DII buying overrode the Wall Street Fed-day selloff and the crude reversal that hit other markets.

items.detail: An **L&T earnings beat and IT bargain-hunting** powered the week's engine — a mid-week surge (the strongest day since June 12) led by Infosys — though **IT reversed to slide more than 2% Friday** as global tech sentiment turned choppy.
items.why: Beaten-down software and capital-goods names drew rotation out of crowded global AI-chip trades, before profit-taking rotated buying into autos and financials.

items.detail: The cheaper-oil tailwind flipped into the market's chief overhang, with **Brent swinging from below $90 to above $88** on a >20% monthly surge as the Strait of Hormuz conflict reignited, while **DIIs (₹2,260 cr Friday) outmuscled cautious FIIs**.
items.why: As a major net crude importer, India faces renewed import-bill, rupee and inflation pressure whenever oil sustains above $90, so domestic institutions had to underpin the bid.

items.detail: **Bitcoin ended the week lower near $62,865** (from ~$64,850 Monday) and **Ether slipped to ~$1,865** (from ~$1,944), failing to reclaim the upper edge of a descending channel.
items.why: Pre-Fed de-risking followed by the hawkish hold and rising Treasury yields kept risk appetite subdued and blocked a bullish breakout.

items.detail: The hawkish Fed plus the re-escalating Middle East oil shock triggered **~$401M in liquidations** (longs ~$298M) and an 11.5% DeFi drop, leaving the **Fear & Greed Index stuck at 28 ('Fear')** all week.
items.why: A hawkish 9–3 hold and a renewed Hormuz-region conflict revived inflation risk simultaneously, keeping speculative capital defensive across the risk curve.

items.detail: Spot Bitcoin ETFs limped to the finish with just **~$205M of net inflows in July — the smallest monthly total on record**, as a mid-month $999M streak was largely undone by ~$526M of late outflows.
items.why: Institutional demand has turned anemic and hedging-driven amid macro stress, following $2.43B of May and $4.52B of June outflows.

crossCuttingTheme: A double macro shock — a hawkish 9–3 Fed hold that drove 30-year yields to 2007 highs and a re-escalating Strait of Hormuz war that flipped Brent from below $90 to a >20% monthly surge — reversed the week's early disinflation optimism, while the AI-capex fault line (Amazon/Microsoft cloud beats vs. Apple/Meta strain) split megacaps, pressured Indian IT and left crypto defensive.
